sections.heading: 1. Two Modes of Reproduction
points: **Reproduction** = the production of new individuals of a species.
**Asexual reproduction** — a **single parent**; offspring are identical to the parent; **no seeds**.
**Sexual reproduction** — involves the **fusion of male and female gametes**; produces **seeds** (in flowering plants).

sections.heading: 2. Asexual Reproduction in Plants
points: **Vegetative propagation** — new plants from roots, stems, leaves or buds (e.g. potato **eyes**, ginger, onion, **Bryophyllum leaf buds**, rose/sugarcane **cuttings**).
**Budding** — a bud grows and detaches (e.g. **yeast**).
**Fragmentation** — the body breaks into pieces that each grow (e.g. **Spirogyra**).
**Spore formation** — tiny **spores** grow into new plants (e.g. **fungi, ferns, mosses**).

sections.heading: 3. Sexual Reproduction — The Flower
points: The **flower** is the reproductive part.
**Stamen** = the **male** part (anther + filament); the anther makes **pollen grains**.
**Pistil/Carpel** = the **female** part (stigma, style, ovary); the ovary contains **ovules**.
**Bisexual flower** = has both stamen and pistil (e.g. mustard); **unisexual** = only one (e.g. papaya, corn).

sections.heading: 4. Pollination, Fertilisation and Seed Dispersal
points: **Pollination** = transfer of **pollen** from anther to stigma. **Self-pollination** (same flower/plant) vs **cross-pollination** (different plant); carried by **wind, water, insects**.
**Fertilisation** = fusion of the **male gamete (in pollen) with the female gamete (egg in ovule)** → forms the **zygote** → seed.
After fertilisation: **ovule → seed**, **ovary → fruit**.
**Seed dispersal** (by wind, water, animals, explosion) spreads seeds, preventing overcrowding and helping new areas.

sections.heading: 5. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: Asexual = one parent, identical offspring (vegetative, budding, fragmentation, spores).
Yeast = budding; Spirogyra = fragmentation; fungi/ferns = spores; Bryophyllum = leaf buds.
Stamen (anther+filament) = male, makes pollen; pistil (stigma-style-ovary) = female, has ovules.
Pollination = pollen to stigma; fertilisation = male + female gamete → zygote.
After fertilisation: ovule → seed, ovary → fruit; seeds dispersed by wind/water/animals.

sections.heading: 6. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: **Pollination** (pollen transfer) is different from **fertilisation** (gamete fusion) — pollination comes first.
**Stamen = male; pistil/carpel = female** part of the flower.
After fertilisation, the **ovary becomes the fruit** and the **ovule becomes the seed**.
**Budding = yeast; fragmentation = Spirogyra; spores = fungi/ferns** — match correctly.
